_meta.rule_under_test: R6 (working standard not referenced) × 2 findings → section ESCALATE
_meta.direction: NEGATIVE (two S.5 findings both FLAG via R6 → both ESCALATE)
_meta.description: Two S.5 findings for a fixed-dose combination product (Amlodipine + Valsartan). Both findings mention lot number, CoA, and source, but neither mentions any form of working standard or secondary standard — the phrases are simply absent from the rationale and evidence. R6 fires on both. Two FLAGs in section 3.2.S.5 triggers the section escalation rule — both promoted to ESCALATE. NOTE: R6 is a keyword-presence check; a rationale that says 'no working standard provided' would still mention the keyword and would NOT trigger R6 — it would instead trigger the upstream S5 completeness check in s5_standards.py.
_meta.author: M5

findings.rationale: Amlodipine Besylate: USP lot R09060 cited as primary reference standard. Certificate of analysis (CoA) submitted with overlaid IR spectra. Source of reference standards: United States Pharmacopeia. USP 47 edition claimed.
findings.evidence_snippet: CoA submitted. Lot no. R09060. Source: USP. Edition USP 47 current at submission date.

findings.rationale: Valsartan: BP lot BP-VAL-2024-003 cited as primary reference standard. Certificate of analysis (CoA) submitted. Source: British Pharmacopoeia Commission. BP 2024 claimed.
findings.evidence_snippet: CoA submitted. Lot no. BP-VAL-2024-003. Source: BP Commission. Edition BP 2024 current.

findings.note: R6 fires: neither 'working standard', 'secondary standard', nor 'ws' appear anywhere in rationale or evidence. Promoted from FLAG to ESCALATE — 2 FLAGs exist in section 3.2.S.5.
R6 fires for the same reason on the second drug substance. Section rule promotes both to ESCALATE.
